_doc:
PR-A+2 fabric harness baseline (Refs #3986-A+2 / #4117).

Records the per-component annual metered energy (heating MWh, cooling
MWh) for each (case × selector) combination exercised by
`tests/all_tests/ashrae_140_fabric_multiselector.rs`. The Python gate
`scripts/check_ashrae_140_fabric_regression.py` compares each
measurement against this baseline and FAILS on regression beyond
`regression_tolerance_rel_pct`.

## What this gate catches (and does NOT catch)

**Catches:**
- Selector wiring drift: a regression that flips the dispatch path on
  one (case, selector) combination. E.g. Case 600 / 9r4c cooling was
  4.858 MWh — if a future change causes it to drop to 2.5 MWh (the
  Case 600 / 5r1c value), the selector no longer matters.
- Selector-parity drift: the `parity` row captures the ratio of
  (FiveROneC value) / (NineRFourC value) for each case. If the
  per-selector wiring is honored end-to-end, this ratio stays
  approximately constant across PRs (it encodes the structural
  physics gap, not a tunable). A 10pp+ ratio shift means a selector
  silently changed paths.

**Does NOT catch:**
- ASHRAE 140 ±15% band violations (Case 600 cooling is known-fail
  per `tests/reference_data/zone_balance/strict_energy_gate_baseline.json`).
  That is `check_strict_energy_gate_regression.py`'s job.
- Absolute-value physics regressions that affect both selectors
  identically (both selectors drift together). The strict-energy-gate
  already catches that for the cases it covers (600/800/810/900/920/
  950/960/970); this baseline intentionally does not duplicate it.

## Why Cases 900 and 950 show identical selector values

Both Case 900 and Case 950 are *high-mass* specs; `from_spec_with_selector`
auto-promotes them to the 9R4C network regardless of the requested
selector (per AGENTS.md ADR-0017 wording: 'HighMass specs still
auto-promote to 9R4C via `from_spec_with_selector`'). The selector
field is therefore informational for these two cases (the engine
ignores the FiveROneC request and runs 9R4C). Case 600 is a
*low-mass* spec where the selector actually drives a different
network — that is why the Case 600 row shows selector divergence.

This is the structural-physics asymmetry the fabric harness makes
explicit: low-mass cases expose selector divergence; high-mass cases
collapse to the auto-promoted network. The Python gate catches both
classes of regression.

## Regenerating the baseline

```
# Re-run the harness and capture the printed lines:
cargo test --release --test all_tests \
    ashrae_140_fabric_multiselector:: -- --nocapture 2>&1 \
    | tee /tmp/fabric_output.txt
# Update this JSON from the captured H/C values; the Python gate
# handles drift detection so a JSON update must be committed WITH the
# engine change that produced the new values (per AGENTS.md 'no
# baseline raising to hide regressions').
python3 scripts/check_ashrae_140_fabric_regression.py \
    /tmp/fabric_output.txt
```
_rule: Per AGENTS.md / RULES.md: this file records the KNOWN values; it must never be raised to hide a regression. Only lower (i.e. record smaller drift / smaller selector-parity delta) when the engine genuinely improved, and commit the improving change together with the baseline update.
captured_commit: feat/per-surface-exterior-boundary-4166 @ d6239be8 + repair (2026-09-28); Case 600/5r1c re-baselined: H 4.901->5.126 MWh (+4.6%), C 2.620->3.456 MWh (+31.9%); both move TOWARD published ASHRAE 140 bands (heating [4314,5836] kWh: 5126 in-band; cooling [3920,6140] kWh: 3456 below-band; lower-bound shortfall reduced 64.3% (1300->464 kWh) vs legacy 2620); 9r4c/900/950 unchanged
_regression_tolerance_rel_pct_doc: Per-measurement relative tolerance (% of recorded value). 10% absorbs floating-point noise from cross-runner builds without masking a real selector-wiring drift. Tighten in a follow-up PR if cross-runner noise is lower than expected.
_regression_tolerance_ratio_abs_doc: Per-case selector-parity ratio tolerance (absolute deviation from baseline ratio). 0.10 = a 10pp shift in the ratio (e.g. baseline ratio 0.54 must stay in [0.44, 0.64]). Absorbs floating-point noise without masking a structural selector-wiring regression.

case_600_5r1c.note: low-mass spec; FiveROneC selector drives 5R1C network; per-surface exterior boundary (Issue #4166, PR #4222) with ASHRAE LW sign (was 4.901/2.620 with legacy lumped SolAirTemperature)

case_600_9r4c.note: low-mass spec; NineRFourC selector drives 9R4C network (diverges from 5R1C, as expected)

case_900_5r1c.note: high-mass spec; FiveROneC selector auto-promoted to 9R4C by from_spec_with_selector (per ADR-0017)

case_900_9r4c.note: high-mass spec; NineRFourC selector drives 9R4C network (identical to 5r1c row by structural auto-promotion)

case_950_5r1c.note: high-mass spec; FiveROneC selector auto-promoted to 9R4C by from_spec_with_selector

case_950_9r4c.note: high-mass spec; NineRFourC selector drives 9R4C network (identical to 5r1c row by structural auto-promotion)

parity_ratios._doc: Recorded selector-parity ratios per case (FiveROneC_value / NineRFourC_value, per metric). Case 600 shows non-unity ratios (5R1C vs 9R4C take different paths for a low-mass spec); Cases 900/950 show exactly 1.0 because high-mass specs auto-promote to 9R4C for both selectors (per ADR-0017). The Python gate bounds the per-case ratio drift against these recorded values.
